study_design: Case-control study of Caucasian prostate cancer cases and controls
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Using a new database, we examined the role of phytoestrogen intake and prostate cancer risk in 83 Caucasian cases and 107 controls.
reason: The case-control study evaluated prostate cancer risk overall and did not define or analyze an aggressive incident prostate cancer endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Genistein, the most studied phytoestrogen, showed a slight protective effect (p = 0.26).
estimate_classifications.reason: The genistein result concerns overall prostate cancer risk and has no aggressive disease restriction.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: However, a positive association was found between campesterol (p = 0.08) and stigmasterol (p = 0.03) and risk of prostate cancer.
estimate_classifications.reason: The plant sterol result concerns overall prostate cancer risk and does not specify aggressive disease.
